Clumsy. Outcast from Otoh Gunga for continually making mistakes that placed other members of Gungan society at risk. |game_text=May deploy to any site, even without presence or Force icons. During battle may use 1 Force to target one opponent's character present. Both players draw destiny. If your destiny + 2 > opponent's destiny + target's ability, Jar Jar and target are lost. |printings='''Decipher''' — '''this page''' (11_4) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Character: Jar Jar Binks, Tatooine, R |strategy=By I-Ming Chenhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/jarjarbinks.html [[Jar Jar Binks]]... What you say !! Everyone hates him, everyone loves him. Will he show up in yousa Light Side deck? Sure, whysa not? The clumsy Gungan can potentially fumble his way into any place, no matter how secure the location may be. He can trip his way into the [[Endor: Bunker]] even if [[Ephant Mon]] is guarding the place. He can waltz right into the Emperor's [[Death Star II: Throne Room]] -- followed by his Enhanced friends with permanent weapons to dispatch the Emperor. Also, Jar Jar's game text can be handy in battle. Just like the movie, he can put someone out of commission. Upset and missing Jar Jar after his latest catastrophe? No problem. Nothing a [[Bacta Tank]] or [[Brisky Morning Munchen]] can't fix. |combos=* [[Jar Jar Binks]] + [[Brisky Morning Munchen]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Jar%20Jar%20Binks Scomp: Jar Jar Binks]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Virtual Modern (ALT)''' — [[Padmé Naberrie (V) (ALT)]] (203_36) |see_also=* [[Padmé Naberrie (AI)]] * [[Alternate Image]] |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Character: Padme Naberrie, Tatooine, R |strategy=By [mailto:jediknight@decipher.com Jedi Knight]https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/padmenaberrie.html Power 3, Ability 3, destiny 3 and Forfeit 5 — all for 2 deploy! Statistics alone are a very solid reason to consider the disguised Queen for your deck! But there's more! For one thing, this version of the Amidala persona is a Republic character, thus unaffected by anything that targets Rebels. For example, [[Charming To The Last]], [[Put All Sections On Alert]] and the popular Scum deck helper, [[None Shall Pass]], all fall flat when faced with this Republican. Of course, her real kicker is in her game text. Besides the fact that her Jedi protectors keep her safe from weapon fire, she can even 'download' them! Twice per game, deploy Qui-Gon or [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] to Padmé's site. That's a very fast way to get out any version of two of your biggest characters. And of course, you could just use it to get Qui-Gon twice to stall an opponent's Hunt Down, or perhaps [[Ben Kenobi]] twice to push your Profit deck along. So what are her disdvantages? Only one, but it is red, black and nasty — [[Darth Maul]] is looking for her. But even then, Padmé benefits — if Dark Side is playing a 'Hunt The Queen' strategy (I Will Find Them Quickly Master and the Epic Event, [[If The Trace Was Correct]]) then she can deploy straight from your Reserve Deck. Padmé — you'll be seeing a lot of her. |combos=* [[Padmé Naberrie]] + [[Jerus Jannick]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Padme%20Naberrie Scomp: Padme Naberrie]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). In addition to the always strong "ordinary" uses, like adding to a Force drain or cleaving targets like a ginsu knife, this elegant tool has a few additional benefits. Many of the new "Jedi helpers" ([[A Jedi's Concentration]], [[A Jedi's Focus]], and [[A Jedi's Patience]]) require your Knight or Master to be armed with a lightsaber, and thus Qui-Gon will be at his most efficient when he has his. Served under Captain Magneta before his current assignment. |game_text=Deploys -1 to same site as Amidala. Once per game, may deploy a blaster on Panaka from Reserve Deck; reshuffle. Once per turn, if Panaka just fired a blaster and 'hit' a character, opponent loses 2 Force. |printings='''Decipher''' — '''this page''' (12_2) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Character: Captain Panaka, Coruscant, R |strategy=By GRSwindlehuhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/coruscant/light/small/captainpanaka.html Finally, they're bringing out the Royal Guards... for the Light Side! Along with her Jedi protectors, this leader of the Queen's Guard is handy to have around – especially to pick off unwanted characters. [[Captain Panaka]] may not have Jedi stats, but his game text and matching weapon say enough. Put [[Panaka's Blaster]] on him and he fires it for free, draws weapon destiny +2, and, if he hits, your opponent loses 2 Force. Pretty sharp shootin'! The real kicker? He gets his matching weapon from Reserve Deck! Now that's card efficiency. His stats are like [[General Solo]] or [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]], making him a strong character. All for deploy of 4, or 3 at Amidala's location, and a forfeit of 6. You might just find a reason to make some room for this sharpshooter – and his gun – in your deck. Combos: Great chance to hit a Dark Jedi with a blaster, nearly impossible to miss others! |combos=* [[Captain Panaka]] + [[Panaka's Blaster]] + [[Blaster Proficiency]]: Great chance to hit a Dark Jedi with a blaster, nearly impossible to miss others.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Captain%20Panaka Scomp: Captain Panaka]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Virtual Original''' — [[Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber (V) (Virtual Set 16: Revenge Of The Sith)]] (1116_29)
'''Virtual Legacy''' — [[Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber (V)]] (1250_72) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Location: Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber, Coruscant, R |strategy=By Doug Taylorhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/coruscant/light/small/coruscantjedicouncilchamber.html It's been 5 years since the game has seen the introduction of a 3/0 location. Back in 1996, the Dark Side got the [[Death Star (Special Edition){{!}}Death Star]] system in [[A New Hope]]. Now, the Light Side gets the first 3/0 site to balance things out. Any location that is so incredible for generating Force serves as a two-edged sword and poses a great danger for the person playing it. One must be extremely cautious to not allow it to fall into enemy hands, lest those 3 icons of Force-generating goodness be turned into a painful Force drain of 3 each turn. Fortunately, this new Light side mega-Force engine is custom-built to be the staging ground for the powerful and mysterious Jedi Council. Most of the Council members are completely immune to attrition there, and many cannot deploy anywhere else. Many of the strongest mechanics of these members (like those of [[Mace Windu]] and [[Depa Billaba]]) function only when that Jedi Master is contemplating the universe from within the sacred chambers. Another great feature of this locale is the ability to "download" [[Yoda, Senior Council Member]], who can then act to disperse your Jedi around the galaxy and augment your forces elsewhere. Combos: Use the Council Chamber as your "other [E1] location" on the Senator Objective to start yourself out with 4 Force icons while giving your opponent only 1. Use this Interrupt to deploy your JCC, or (once it's out) to get those Jedi Council members out of your deck and into the Council Chamber where they belong. |combos=* [[Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber]] + [[Plead My Case To The Senate / Sanity And Compassion{{!}}Plead My Case To The Senate]] Objective[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Coruscant%3A%20Jedi%20Council%20Chamber Scomp: Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec).
